title: I can't open powertoys settings by double clicking

judgment.rationale: The report belongs with the existing Windows 10 PowerToys UI-launch investigation in #40234 rather than a separate fix queue. The symptom is the same Settings process failure, the reporter's CET/runtime findings add useful diagnostic evidence, and a PowerToys collaborator already closed the closely matching #41292 as a duplicate of #40234. No public PowerToys change was found that fixes Settings specifically.
evidence: The issue body reports PowerToysUserSetup-0.101.2432.0-x64 on Windows 10 where double-clicking the icon does not open Settings, while the same action works on Windows 11.

The reporter later supplied Event Viewer and runtime tracing details: PowerToys.Settings.exe exits with 0x80131506 (COR_E_EXECUTIONENGINE) in KERNELBASE.dll before PowerToys logs are created, and disabling Hardware-enforced Stack Protection or updating Windows restores launch.

A second commenter reports the same CET-related failure pattern for PowerToys.FancyZonesEditor.exe, showing that the evidence concerns the Windows 10 WinUI/.NET executable family rather than only one Settings click path.
Open issue #40234 tracks the matching Windows 10 behavior where PowerToys remains running but Settings, Quick Access, and other UI windows fail to appear.
Collaborator Niels9001 closed #41292 as a duplicate of #40234, explicitly identifying the same PowerToys Settings UI launch failure.

Open issue #47814 separately records a Windows 10 CET/coreclr startup failure when User Shadow Stack is enabled, corroborating the relevance of CET compatibility but not establishing a separate PowerToys fix.
Merged PR #37550 disables CETCompat only for the PowerToys Run launcher and does not cover PowerToys.Settings.exe or FancyZonesEditor.exe.

Repository UI-test guidance states that Windows 10 below the documented CET servicing floor can fail with 0x80131506; this supports the runtime hypothesis but is not a maintainer-confirmed resolution for this issue.
judgment.recommended_action: Consolidate this report with the active canonical investigation #40234 and carry over the reporter's CET evidence there; do not start a competing Settings-specific implementation until maintainers determine whether the shared UI-launch failure needs a product change.

confidence.rationale: The duplicate relationship is supported by the matching public symptom, explicit collaborator duplicate handling for #41292, and the active #40234 investigation. The CET explanation is retained as evidence and an inference, not treated as a confirmed root cause.

fix_assessment.rationale: A separate PowerToys code fix is not applicable to this report while the matching public investigation remains active and the available evidence points to a shared Windows 10 UI/runtime launch condition. The existing CETCompat change is limited to PowerToys Run and is not an existing fix for Settings or FancyZones.

issue_context.summary: On Windows 10, PowerToys UI executables can start and exit without displaying a window. The reporter's crash evidence points to a CET/.NET runtime interaction, and a second user reproduced the mitigation behavior on FancyZones, so this report should enrich the active shared investigation rather than create a competing fix.
known_information: The reported package is PowerToysUserSetup-0.101.2432.0-x64 installed from GitHub.
Settings opens on the reporter's Windows 11 laptop but not on the Windows 10 machine.
Event Viewer reports PowerToys.Settings.exe failing with exception code 0x80131506 (COR_E_EXECUTIONENGINE) in KERNELBASE.dll.
The reporter says the process exits before PowerToys logs are generated.
The reporter says Windows updates or disabling Hardware-enforced Stack Protection for PowerToys.Settings.exe restores launch.
A second commenter reports the same workaround pattern for PowerToys.FancyZonesEditor.exe.
Issue #40234 is open with the same Windows 10 UI-launch symptom, and #41292 was closed by a collaborator as its duplicate.
Issue #47814 is an open related report describing a Windows 10 CET/coreclr startup failure.
PR #37550 is merged but changes CETCompat only for the PowerToys Run launcher.
inferences: The Settings and FancyZones results are likely part of the same Windows 10 WinUI/.NET executable startup failure family, but the exact failing runtime branch is not confirmed by a PowerToys maintainer.

The reported workaround and the repository's CET servicing guidance make an OS/runtime compatibility condition plausible, but they do not prove that every affected Windows 10 build has the same cause.
Because #40234 already covers the shared UI-launch symptom, maintaining a separate implementation plan for #50335 would risk duplicating triage and splitting evidence.
issue_context.analysis: The newest comment materially strengthens the report: it confirms that the failure is not limited to one Settings invocation and that the same exploit-protection mitigation affects another PowerToys WinUI executable. Public repository evidence also shows that PowerToys routes UI launch through executable startup and that the merged CETCompat precedent is scoped only to PowerToys Run. The most reliable maintainer action is therefore to link the detailed CET evidence to #40234, which is the active canonical investigation for the same Windows 10 UI-launch family, while keeping the CET mechanism explicitly qualified as an inference.

comment.body: Thanks for documenting the 0x80131506 crash and the Hardware-enforced Stack Protection workaround, and for confirming that the same behavior affects another PowerToys UI executable. This report matches the active Windows 10 UI-launch investigation in #40234, where Settings and other PowerToys UI windows fail to appear while PowerToys remains running. A collaborator closed the closely matching #41292 as a duplicate of #40234. Please add the detailed CET/runtime findings from this report to #40234 so the investigation has the Event Viewer result, workaround, and second-executable confirmation in one place. The merged CETCompat change in #37550 is scoped to PowerToys Run and does not establish a fix for Settings.
